definitions.explanation: To place something into an opening or container.
To insert a cutting into soil or another plant.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}を{花瓶|かびん}に{挿|さ}す。
examples.english: To put flowers in a vase.

examples.japanese: コンセントを{挿|さ}して{電気|でんき}をつけた。
examples.english: I plugged it in and turned on the power.

examples.japanese: {髪|かみ}にかんざしを{挿|さ}すと、とても{きれい}に{見|み}える。
examples.english: When you put a hairpin in your hair, it looks very pretty.

examples.japanese: パソコンにUSBメモリを{挿|さ}して、{写真|しゃしん}のデータを{移|うつ}した。
examples.english: I inserted a USB drive into the computer and transferred the photo data.
To insert a cutting into soil.

examples.japanese: {挿|さ}し{木|き}で{植物|しょくぶつ}を{増|ふ}やす。
{芽|め}を{土|つち}に{挿|さ}して{水|みず}をやると、やがて{根|ね}が{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: If you insert a shoot into soil and water it, roots will eventually grow.

examples.japanese: バラの{枝|えだ}を{切|き}って{挿|さ}し{木|き}にしたら、うまく{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: I cut a rose branch and made a cutting from it, and it grew well.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になったら{挿|さ}し{木|き}をして、{庭|にわ}の{花|はな}を{増|ふ}やそうと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: When spring comes, I plan to do some cuttings and increase the flowers in the garden.

notes:
{挿|さ}す means to insert or put something into an opening, slot, or container.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle for the object being inserted

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {花|はな}を{花瓶|かびん}に{挿|さ}す: to put flowers in a vase
- {鍵|かぎ}を{挿|さ}す: to insert a key
- コンセントを{挿|さ}す: to plug in
- {髪|かみ}に{挿|さ}す: to put (ornament) in one's hair

COMPOUNDS:
- {挿|さ}し{木|き}: plant cutting (for propagation)
- {挿|さ}し{絵|え}: illustration (inserted in text)

KANJI DISTINCTION:
Several verbs read さす use different kanji:
- {挿|さ}す: to insert
- {刺|さ}す: to stab, pierce
- {指|さ}す: to point
- {差|さ}す: to hold up (umbrella)
- {射|さ}す: (light) to shine
